Description:
Number of SDCCH transactions that are ended because of a failure in the Abis interface during a call in progress. There is no acknowledgement of channel activation, no indication of call establishment received, i.e., ghosts.

Impact: Call cleared

Reason for the impact: External / Abis interface
Updated:
When an SDCCH transaction ends because of signalling problems in the Abis interface and the RRM releases the SDCCH. 

This counter is updated in call phases 1-8 only.

Reasons that trigger the counter: 
- Phantom RACHs that have a valid establishment cause. 
- The BTS can hear the MS, but the MS cannot hear the BTS, and so the MS does not respond to the IMMEDIATE ASSIGNMENT message with a SABM. 
- MS is accessing the network at the limit of sensitivity and messages are lost. 
- Poor Radio conditions. 
- MS is accessing network through another BTS (co-channel, co-BSIC interference). 

See figures: 
- Unsuccessful SDCCH activation, timer expires while waiting for CHANNEL_ACTIVATION_ACK message 
- Unsuccessful SDCCH activation, timer expires while waiting for PHYSICAL_CONTEXT_CONFIRM message 
- TRX/TSL is blocked with different causes during an SDCCH channel activation

Network Element Name: TCH REQUEST REJECTED DUE TO LACK
Description:
Number of requests for TCHs that are rejected because there are no radio resources available. All kinds of procedures used to request a TCH are considered, that is, the TCH is rejected if there is no requested resources available for assignments using the normal TCH assignment procedure and assignments for all kinds of (incoming) handovers. This counter is also updated when a request for TCH is rejected because of a mismatch between the types of the requested channel and the A interface circuit.

See also counter 004079.
Updated:
When the RRM has no TCHs available for either call or HO attempt
requests, or the RRM changes the A interface circuit pool before the TCH allocation.
This counter may be updated immediately after a TCH request or, in case of queuing,when the queuing timer expires.
NOTE! In case of DR this counter is updated as follows:
1) When a call is removed from the queue because of a DR attempt, this counter is
NOT updated on the SOURCE side, instead counter 001173 is updated.
2) If queuing is not used or the queuing timer expires before a DR attempt, this
counter is updated on the SOURCE side.
3) On the TARGET side, this counter is updated in case of congestion (blocking).
See figures:
- Basic call without counters
- Basic call, no free TCHs, unsuccessful queuing and directed retry not activated
- TCH assignment failure with cause switch_circuit_pool, queuing and directed retry not allowed
- Unsuccessful underlay overlay internal intra-cell handover, queuing not allowed
- Internal intra-cell handover, unsuccessful TCH queuing
- Unsuccessful forced release
- Unsuccessful forced release with external handover
- Unsuccessful forced handover

For example, RACHs from different MSs can clash and cause a high signal level, but the decoding does not find any detectable RACH. The interference causes lots of bursts that trigger the counter, but these bursts are then filtered out in the detection.

Description:
Average number of busy RACHs on a CCCH.

Counter 003015 is updated along with this counter.
Updated:
When the value of the RACH load is received in a CCCH_LOAD_INDICATION message from the BTS during a measurement period. The number of busy RACHs is added to the previous value and the number of the events is increased by one.

NOTE! This RACH counter is triggered when the RX Level is above -100dBm. Other detection methods (like CRC or S/N) are not applied. This means that high load on RACH may occure even without a significant number of CHANNEL_REQUIRED messages. For example, RACHs from different MSs can clash and cause a high signal level, but the decoding does not find any detectable RACH. The interference causes lots of bursts that trigger the counter, but these bursts are then filtered out in the detection.

See figure CCCH load indication.

Uplink quality 00000000000000010000000000000000

Uplink strength 00000000000001000000000000000000
Downlink quality 00000000000010000000000000000000

Downlink strength 00000000001000000000000000000000

Description:
Sum of TRX specific downlink RF power level value samples in the serving cell. The value range of a single RF power level sample is 0...15. 

RF power level value mapping (Pmax is the maximum transmission power of the BTS): 
0 -> Pmax - 0 dBm 
1 -> Pmax - 2 dBm 
2 -> Pmax - 4 dBm 
... 
15 -> Pmax - 30 dBm. 

If Pmax is 43 dBm, then the value 0 means 43 dBm and the value 15 means 13 dBm. 

The average TRX specific downlink RF power level used in the cell can be calculated by dividing this counter with the denominator counter 005007 POWER DENOMINATOR 2.
Updated:
The RF power level value is sampled every 20 seconds during a call.
Note: Counter will not be updated for a call, if the latest Measurement report received before expiry of the internal timer has UL/DL Rxlevel as ZERO. Impact: Less pegging for the mentioned counters in BSC17/BSc18 w.r.t BSC16 KPI.

Network Element Name: AMR FR CODEC MODE 3 ON UPLINK DIRECTION WITH RXQUAL 4
Description:
Number of AMR FR codec mode 3 usage on uplink direction within RxQual 4. On fast link adaptation (LA) mode the codec mode is the last codec mode used during the radio link measurement interval. On slow LA mode this counter indicates the only used codec mode on the radio link measurement interval.

Counter 014149 AMR CODEC MODE SETS is updated along with this counter.
Updated: The number of usages are sampled when MEASUREMENT RESULT messages are received. The Radio Connection Supervision receives a radio measurement from the BTS which indicates that the AMR FR codec mode 3 is used as an uplink codec mode at the end of the radio link measurement interval. The counter is updated with sampled data at the end of the call or when the handover is performed.

Description:
Calculation result of location estimate. The field is union-type and fields in the result-counter depend on the value of shape field.

Length : byte 
Length of the longest possible field, though the actual number of bytes in use depends on the value of shape field

Shape: byte 
0b0001 Ellipsoid point with uncertainty circle
0b0010 Ellipsoid point with uncertainty ellipse
0b1001 Ellipsoid point with altitude and uncertainty ellipsoid
0b1010 Ellipsoid arc

Different types are according to the shape-field value the following:

In case of 0b0001 Ellipsoid point with uncertainty circle:
Sign of latitude: byte
Degrees of latitude: dword
Degrees of longitude: longint
Uncertainty code: byte

In case of 0b0010 Ellipsoid point with uncertainty ellipse:
Sign of latitude: byte
Degrees of latitude: dword
Degrees of longitude: longint
Uncertainty semi-major axis: byte
Uncertainty semi-minor axis: byte
Angle of major axis: byte
Confidence: byte

In case of 0b1001 Ellipsoid point with altitude and uncertainty ellipsoid:
Sign of latitude: byte
Degrees of latitude: dword
Degrees of longitude: longint
Altitude: word
Uncertainty semi-major axis: byte
Uncertainty semi-minor axis: byte
Angle of major axis: byte
Uncertainty altitude: byte
Confidence: byte

In case of 0b1010 Ellipsoid arc:
Sign of latitude: byte
Degrees of latitude: dword
Degrees of longitude: longint
Inner radius: word
Uncertainty radius: byte
Offset angle: byte
Included angle: byte
Confidence: byte

Description: Number of TCH requests.
Updated:
On a regular TRX:
- when the RRM receives a TCH request either in a call or HO attempt

NOTE! A BTS can have more than one regular TRX, but this counter is updated merely on one regular TRX of the BTS.

On a super-reuse TRX:
This counter increases by one when the Radio Resource Management receives a TCH request either in a call (underlay - overlay assignment or direct access) or in a handover attempt to a super-reuse TRX, and the TRX in question is one of the candidates in the target TRX list.

NOTE! This counter is updated on every super-reuse TRX which is on the target TRX list in an HO attempt to a super-reuse TRX.

The counter update is visible in all figures of 52 Underlay-Overlay Statistics Measurement except for the following:

Description: Number of the TCH new call assignments.
Updated:
When an ASSIGNMENT_COMPLETE message is received on TCH from the BTS in a case of a new call. In a case of FACCH call set-up due to SDCCH congestion, this counter is updated, when an ESTABLISH_INDICATION message is received on the TCH from the BTS. In case of normal directed retry (inter-cell directed retry), this counter is updated, when a HANDOVER_COMPLETE message is received on the TCH from the BTS. This counter is also updated with S6 feature TCH Assignment to Super-reuse TRX in IUO (intra-cell/inter-cell directed retry) and with S7 feature Direct Access to Super-reuse TRX in IUO. If external SDCCH to SDCCH handover is made after a re-establishment, this counter is also updated.

Description: The number of successful uplink TBF reallocations.
Updated:
When new resources are allocated for an uplink TBF, for example, when the number of TSLs for an existing TBF is changed. A TBF receives a new TFI when, and only when, it is reallocated. The reallocation is detected from the changed TFI, that is, neither the channels that are used, nor their number does necessarily have to change in reallocation. 

Other possible reasons for reallocation include, for example: 
- territory downgrades (CSW traffic)
- the establishment of simultaneous TBFs to downlink
- the availability of better resources on other channels
- a change of requirements from the MS.

The PCU can change the uplink TCH configuration at any time by sending the MS a PACKET_UPLINK_ASSIGNMENT or a PACKET_TIMESLOT_RECONFIGURE message. If the reallocation is impossible, for example, in a GPRS territory downgrade, the PCU can release a TBF with a PDCH_RELEASE message. 

This counter is updated separately for normal, extended and super-extended areas.

Network Element Name: REQ UL TBF DURING DL TBF
Description: The number of uplink TBF establishment requests during a downlink TBF.
Updated:
When an uplink TBF is requested during a downlink TBF. The MS can request resources for an uplink TBF by including a Channel Request Description IE in the PACKET_DOWNLINK_ACK/NACK message. If there is no need to change the downlink TCH configuration, the PACKET_DOWNLINK_ASSIGNMENT message is used to tell the uplink TCH configuration and USF values of each TCH and TFI to the MS.
If the downlink TCH configuration is changed, a PACKET_TIMESLOT_RECONFIGURE message is used to tell the MS both the uplink and downlink TCH configuration and USF values of the uplink TCHs as well as the uplink and downlink TFIs. The procedure is complete when the first block on the assigned uplink TCH is received. This procedure is guarded by a timer. If the PACKET_UPLINK_ASSIGNMENT fails, the uplink TBF is released. If the PACKET_TIMESLOT_RECONFIGURE fails, both the downlink and uplink TBFs are released.

Network Element Name: AVE DOWNL SIGNAL STRENGTH IN ADJ CELL 2
Description: Average strength of the downlink signal received from an adjacent cell 2. The values range from 0 to 73. The denominator is the sum of counters 075015, 075016 and 075017.
Updated:
When the MS reports an adjacent cell during a call, the strength of the received signal of the defined adjacent cell is registered. The average strength of the downlink signal from the adjacent cell is calculated on the basis of these records. 
Strength of the received signal level according to 3GPP TS 05.08 (8.1.4): 
0 = less than -110 dBm 
1 = between -110 and -109 dBm 
2 = between -109 and -108 dBm 
... 
72 = between -39 and -38 dBm 
73 = greater than -38 dBm

Description:

Network Element Name: NBR OF EST DL FER CL 4
Description: Number of estimated DL FER samples in class 4.
Updated:
When the BTS reports DL BER value in the radio link measurement report, the BSC maps it to estimated class 4 DL FER value with the help of a correlation table. The number of times, when DL BER value is estimated to class 4 DL FER value, is updated to the counter at the end of the call or when the handover is performed. If the BSC is not able to create the correlation table for the used codec, that is, the BSC hasn't received enough UL FER, UL BER and DL BER values, this counter is not updated.

When the real DL FER value is available, this counter is not updated, but the corresponding real DL FER counter 077027 NBR OF DL FER CL 4 is updated instead.

Description: Number of times a TBF establishment is rejected due to the QoS based Admission Control procedure.
Updated:
This counter is updated whenever the QoS based AC fails due to the fact that the capacity that the TBF would get per timeslot is less than a given parameter threshold value.
Note: The capacity is shared among the users with respect to their weights. Description: Number of times the QoS based Admission Control check is done at TBF establishment.
Updated:
This counter is updated whenever PCU starts the QoS based AC procedure at TBF establishment.

In DL direction the QoS based AC procedure is started when a new DL TBF needs to be established and when the DL-UNITDATA PDU has the T-bit value of 1 (it indicates that the PDU carries user data and not GMM/SM signaling).

In UL direction the QoS based AC procedure is started when

a) One-phase access: MS sends EGPRS PACKET CHANNEL REQUEST message with access type = 'One Phase Access Request' and with Radio Priority larger than zero.

b) Two-phase access: MS sends PACKET RESOURCE REQUEST message with access type = 'Two Phase Access Request' and with Radio Priority larger than zero.

c) DTM request: MS sends DTM REQUEST message with Packet Establishment Cause = User data and with Radio Priority field larger than zero.

Description:
Total sum of FEP values over the measurement period, based on C/I ratios between the serving cell and the adjacent cell 59 that have been corrected by 18 dB. 

Total FEP adjacent channel = SUM( FEP( RXLev_serv + 2 * BS_Power + 18 dB -RXLev_adj) ) 

where: 
- BS_Power is the number of 2dB power control steps from the nominal power level of the serving cell
- RXLev_serv is  RXLevel (-110 dBm -47 dBm) of serving cell
- RXLev_adj is RXLevel (-110 dBm -47 dBm) of adjacent cell 

In case of an overflow in the BCSU/BCXU, the value of this counter is set to FFFF FFFE. In case of an overflow in the OMU, the value is set to FFFF FFFF.
Updated: Whenever the MS reports a serving cell during a call.

Network Element Name: UL DTM TBF DROPS DUE DOWNGRADE
Description: Number of uplink DTM TBFs released due to a territory downgrade procedure.
Updated: When a successfully established uplink TBF operating in dual transfer mode needs to be abnormally released due to a territory downgrade or channel release procedure.
Internal Information:
'Successfully established' means here that the UL TBF has been assigned to the MS with a DTM ASSIGNMENT COMMAND, PACKET ASSIGNMENT, PACKET UPLINK ASSIGNMENT or PACKET TIMESLOT RECONFIGURE message and the PCU has received a valid RLC block from the MS after the assignment on the new resources so that the UL TBF assignment procedure can be considered successfully completed.
'Abnormally released due to territory downgrade or channel release procedure' means that the PCU has received a psw_territory_downgrade_s or psw_channel_release_s message, respectively, that has affected the timeslots where the MS was having a DTM allocation and this has triggered a reallocation attempt for the DTM call which (i.e. the reallocation attempt) failed resulting in the fact that the PCU was forced to cut off the UL RLC data transfer and release the resources reserved for the UL TBF even if the UL data transfer was still ongoing.
'Affects the timeslots where the MS was having a DTM allocation' means here that at least one of the timeslots that has been reserved for the DTM call (this can be a DTM-PS timeslot or a DTM-CS timeslot) needs to be disconnected from PS use, if not yet disconnected, and moved from the PS territory to the CS territory. 
'Failed reallocation attempt' means here that the PCU was not able to find new resources for the MS by means of DTM-PS and/or DTM-CS reallocation procedure and for this reason the UL DTM TBF had to be released.'Cut off the RLC data transfer' means here that the PCU ends the USF scheduling for the UL TBF.
'Release the resources reserved for the UL TBF' means here that the radio resource allocation and other reservations the PCU has made internally for the UL TBF are cleared/released by the PCU.'
Even if the UL data transfer was still ongoing' means here that the PCU had not yet started the normal UL TBF release procedure, i.e, the PCU had not yet sent the PACKET UPLINK ACK/NACK message with FAI bit set to '1' to the MS.
If the DTM-PS reallocation procedure, that was triggered by the territory downgrade or channel release procedure, succeeds and if the PCU is able to send a PACKET UPLINK ASSIGNMENT or PACKET TIMESLOT RECONFIGURE message to the MS on the PACCH channel, then this counter shall NOT be incremented even if the re-assignment procedure later fails (i.e. the PCU does not receive a valid RLC block from the MS on the new resources).
If the DTM-CS reallocation procedure, that was triggered by the territory downgrade or channel release procedure, succeeds and if the PCU is able to send a dtm_establ_req_s message to the DX side, then this counter shall NOT be incremented even if the re-assignment procedure later fails (i.e. the PCU does not receive a valid RLC block from the MS on the new resources or the PCU receives a dtm_alloc_abort_s or dtm_reallo_failure_s or dtm_imsi_exit_ind_s message from the DX during the DTM re-assignment procedure, i.e. after sending the dtm_establ_req_s message and before receiving the dtm_cs_release_req_s message for the source DTM-CS timeslot).
The PCU shall NOT increment this counter if the UL DTM TBF is released due to a DTM call release procedure triggered by dtm_release_req_s or dtm_imsi_exit_ind_s message even if the DTM call release procedure takes place while the territory downgrade or channel release procedure is being processed.The PCU shall NOT increment this counter if the UL DTM TBF is released abnormally due to some other reason (e.g. the counter N3101 reaches its maximum value) even if the abnormal release takes place while the territory downgrade or channel release procedure is being processed

Network Element Name: IBHO ATT TO UTRAN DEFAULT ANE
Description:
The number of IMSI-based handover attempts from the GSM to the default authorised network because of coverage of UTRAN cell of an equivalent PLMN.

The default authorised network is used for an unidentified subscriber. This means that the corresponding subscriber group could not find the subscriber.

Failure of the attempts can be seen in the counter IBHO UNS TO UTRAN DEFAULT ANE of the IBHO measurement. Corresponding handover counters in HO measurement are updated normally in addition to this counter.
Updated: At the source BTS/segment when IMSI-based handover from the GSM to the UTRAN default authorised network is started. It is indicated with the constant def_ane_counter_upd_c in ANE identifier field.

Description: Number of errored blocks (EB) based on the definition at RFC 5086 in accordance with ITU-T G.826. EBs are blocks of data played out to the TDM attachment circuit that have experienced at least one error event. An error event is the loss of a packet, leading to inability to play out payload data at the TDM attachment circuit for the time duration of the lost payload.
Updated:
Number of EBs get measured within a one-second period. 

The EBs are approximated based on the following formulae: 
round up ((number of lost packets * number of frames/ packet) /8).

The counter is incremented with the result of the calculation.
Features: - BSS21157 (Integrated IP card for BSC and TCSM)
Internal Information: Errored blocks shall be counted according to the definition of errored block definition at CESoPSN standard.? A CESoPSN errored data block is defined as a block of data played out to the TDM attachment circuit and of size defined in accordance with the [G.826] rules for the corresponding TDM service that has experienced at least one CESoPSN error event In case of PW packet payload sizes not matching TDM block size, the following formulae shall be applied: round up ((# of frames/packet)*(packet loss/sec) / 8 = (EBs/sec))

round up ((number of lost packets * number of frames/ packet) /8).

Description: Number of downlink RTP packets, containing TRAU frames of circuit switched U-plane, lost based on missing sequence number. This counter does not include those received too early or late.
Updated:
When the next sequence number is missing from downlink RTP packet containing TRAU frames of circuit switched U-plane. If the gap in the RTP sequence numbers is less than a given threshold value (100), then the counter is incremented by the amount of missing RTP packets.
If the gap in the RTP sequence numbers is larger than or equal to the threshold value (100), then it is interpreted that there is a jump in the RTP sequence numbers (might happen e.g. when some NE conducts a switchover) and in this case the counter is not updated.
Features:
- BSS21454 (Packet Abis over IP/Ethernet)
- BSS21440 (Packet Abis over TDM)
Internal Information:
An example: when packets are received with sequence numbers SN1, SN4, SN5 the counter is incremented with 2.

Description: Number of uplink RTP packets containing TRAU frames of circuit switched U-plane, lost based on missing sequence number.
Updated:
When the next sequence number is missing from uplink RTP packet containing TRAU frames of circuit switched U-plane. If the gap in the RTP sequence numbers is less than a given threshold value (100), then the counter is incremented by the amount of missing RTP packets. 
If the gap in the RTP sequence numbers is larger than or equal to the threshold value (100), then it is interpreted that there is a jump in the RTP sequence numbers (might happen e.g. when some NE conducts a switchover) and in this case the counter is not updated.
Features:
- BSS21454 (Packet Abis over IP/Ethernet)
- BSS21440 (Packet Abis over TDM)
Internal Information:
An example: when packets are received with sequence numbers SN1, SN4, SN5 the counter is incremented with 2.
U-plane supervision dummy packets are NOT included. Dummy packets are included into UDP counters that causes minor deviation to multiplexing ratio KPI. The error is per mille that is acceptable.
Document Comments:
V. 1.0 > 1.0. Janne Rissanen: added time/network aggregation function.

Description: Number of times AMR FR 7.95 kbit/s codec mode (bitrate) is used when the RX quality is within class 6 on the downlink direction for an OSC double full rate call. Description:
The sum of Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR).
The counter reports the sum of VSWR value samples taken every 1 minute during the measurement period. Transmitted power and reflected power interferes and forms a standing wave. The VSWR is defined as the ratio of maximum to minimum in this wave. VSWR = (transmitted power + reflected power)/ (transmitted power -reflected power). If the VSWR value is unreliable for the whole period, the value is set to 0xFF. An actual measured VSWR value is reported as multiplied with 10. Unreliable conditions are invalid VSWR alarm, TX low power alarm, VSWR minor alarm or VSWR major alarm. Average value is calculated by dividing the value of this counter by the value of the counter 142005.

In a case of a new call or re-establishment on node of CMST cell, the counter is updated once the MEASUREMENT RESULT message is received after the ASSIGNMENT COMPLETE the first time on TCH from the BTS.
In a case of FACCH call set-up due to SDCCH congestion, the counter is updated, when an ESTABLISH INDICATION message is received on the TCH from the BTS.

Description: Minimum of the ToP phase synchronization error during output interval.
Updated:
The phase synchronization error is sampled once per minute. The counter is updated by the minimum value sampled during the output interval.
The phase error is an estimation of the actual phase error between the secondary BCF and the master clock BCF using BSS ToP as a BSS synchronization source. If  the value is positive, the secondary BCF is leading the master clock BCF, and if the value is negative, the secondary BCF is lagging the master clock BCF.
Internal Information: The counter is updated with the minimum value sampled during the output interval plus 10 000 000. Note that if the value is negative, the value is <10 000 000. The offset of 10 000 000 is removed when storing value into NetAct database. Hence value is signed integer in NetAct.

Description: Maximum of the ToP phase synchronization error during output interval.
Updated:
The phase synchronization error is sampled once per minute. The counter is updated by the maximum value sampled during the output interval.
The phase error is an estimation of the actual phase error between the secondary BCF and the master clock BCF using BSS ToP as a BSS synchronization source. If  the value is positive, the secondary BCF is leading the master clock BCF, and if the value is negative, the secondary BCF is lagging the master clock BCF.
Internal Information: The counter is updated with the maximum value sampled during the output interval plus 10 000 000. Note that if the value is negative, the value is <10 000 000.The offset of 10 000 000 is removed when storing value into NetAct database. Hence value is signed integer in NetAct.

Description: The number of lost DL RTP packets that are not received according to received sequence numbers.

monitoring using Bit Interleaved Parity 8 (BIP-8) code, in an even
parity. The BIP-8 is computed over all the bits of the previous virtual
container/virtual tributary (VC-12 over VC-3 or VC-12 over VC-4
according to the configuration) and is placed in byte B3 of the current
frame. In this case the block means virtual container/virtual tributary.

not updated during the SES and UAS conditions.

Network Element Name: PATH TERMINATION SECTION 2 BACKGROUND BLOCK ERRORS AT THE FAR END
Description:
An errored block is a block in which one or more bits have an error.
G1 byte in the SOH is used for path termination section error
monitoring using Bit Interleaved Parity 8 (BIP-8) code, in an even
parity. The BIP-8 is computed over all bits of the previous virtual
container/virtual tributary (VC-12 over VC-3 or VC-12 over VC-4
according to configuration) and is placed in byte B3 of the current
frame. In this case the block means virtual container/virtual tributary.
Updated:
The counter is incremented when one or more bit errors are
detected in a block (virtual container/virtual tributary). The counter is
not updated during the SES and UAS conditions.

Description:
Multiplex section line background block errors at the near end. An
errored block is a block in which one or more bits have an error. B2
byte in the section overhead header (SOH) is used for Multiplex

code, in an even parity. The BIP-24 is computed over all the bits of
the previous STM frame, excluding RSOH, and is placed in byte B2
of the current frame before scrambling. In this case the block means
STM-1/OC3 frame.

detected in a block (STM-1/OC3 frame, excluding Regenerator
Section / Section Overhead (RSOH/SOH)). The counter is not
updated during the SES and Unavailable Seconds (UAS) conditions.
